fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Luke says Jesus "…went out to the mountain to pray…" Earlier, some people "were filled with rage" (Luke 6:11), and in those days Jesus heads off to pray to God. I think that tells you where He turns first.
Fasting is a fair guess, baker. But Luke says Jesus went out to the mountain to pray. Fasting isn't mentioned in this passage.
Prophets is a fair guess, baker, but it's not the one here. Luke says Jesus designated the twelve as apostles. That's the word to remember for this group.
Elders is a fair guess, baker, but it's not the one in this verse. Luke says Jesus designated the twelve He chose as apostles. That's the title for this team.
Silas isn't in this list of twelve, baker. Luke says Simon is the one "…whom He named Peter…" So Peter is the new name Jesus gives him.
That's what the text says, baker. Luke ends the list with "…Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor." This one is heavy to read. The writer tells us this about him right there in the list.
Tax collector isn't what Luke says about Judas Iscariot, baker. The text says he "…became a traitor." It's a heavy line, so take your time with it.
Fisherman isn't what Luke says about him, baker. Here the text says Judas Iscariot "…became a traitor." That's a heavy thing to find at the end of a list of names.
Yes, baker. Luke says "They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases…" They came for two things: to hear Him and to be healed. That's the reason the text gives for this crowd.

That sounds like the scene just before, baker, where some people discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus (Luke 6:11). But here Luke says the people "…had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases…" That's the reason the text gives for this crowd.
That's right, baker. Luke says "…those troubled by unclean spirits were healed." It sits right there next to the diseases. And Luke says power was coming from Him and healing them all.
